about: The machine and software the 2026-10-28 load test ran on (results in the files beside this one). Read from the live cluster and Google Cloud after the test; the cluster has not been rebuilt since it was created on 2026-10-24, and the node was created 2026-10-26 (a node auto-upgrade). Account, project and address identifiers are left out on purpose.

how_collected.vm: gcloud compute instances describe <node> --zone asia-south1-a (cpuPlatform, disks, scheduling)
how_collected.node: kubectl get node -o json (labels, nodeInfo, capacity, allocatable)
how_collected.volumes: kubectl get pvc,storageclass; gcloud compute disks list
how_collected.workloads: kubectl get pods -o json (images, requests, limits)
docs_checked_2026-10-29: https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/cpu-platforms (Broadwell: Intel Xeon E5 v4, E5-2696V4, base 2.2 GHz, all-core turbo 2.8 GHz, single-core turbo 3.7 GHz; supported by E2 and N1; 'each hardware thread is called a virtual CPU (vCPU)')

https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/general-purpose-machines (e2-standard-2 is 2 vCPUs and 8 GB; E2 offers Intel and AMD EPYC processors and 'the processor is selected for you at the time of VM creation')

google_cloud.product: Google Kubernetes Engine, Standard mode (not Autopilot), zonal cluster
google_cloud.networking: VPC-native (alias IPs), default network and subnet, IPv4 only; NodeLocal DNS cache enabled; network policy disabled; nothing in the cluster has a public address, the only way in is a Cloudflare Tunnel (not used by the load test)
google_cloud.maintenance_window: daily, 21:30 UTC for 4 hours (03:00 to 07:00 IST)
google_cloud.logging_and_monitoring: system components only; the cluster runs its own Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Alloy

node.cpu_platform: Intel Broadwell (as reported by Compute Engine; the exact processor inside the VM was not read)
node.provisioning: STANDARD (not Spot or preemptible), on host maintenance MIGRATE, automatic restart on
node.shielded_vm: integrity monitoring and vTPM on, secure boot off
node.reserved_by_gke_and_system: about 70 millicores of CPU and 1.87 GiB of memory (capacity minus allocatable)

software.services: 8 Go services, Go toolchain 1.27.3 (golang:1.27.3-bookworm), go.mod 'go 1.27.2', static binaries in gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
software.kafka: 4.3.1, KRaft, one node (broker and controller), heap -Xmx512M -Xms512M, three topics of 3 partitions with replication factor 1

monitoring.prometheus: v3.15.0 (scrape and rule interval 30 s, retention 15 days or 8 GiB)

software.tunnel: cloudflared 2026.10.2 (two replicas; not in the test's path)

workloads_on_the_node_during_the_test.note: One replica of everything. Requests and limits as deployed. No service has a CPU limit; every container has a memory limit.

rows.name: k6 load generator (a Job per level)

test_setup.generator: k6 as a Kubernetes Job on the same node, calling the gateway service directly inside the cluster (no Cloudflare, no internet)
test_setup.per_level: 30 s ramp up, 120 s hold, 15 s ramp down, one Job per level
test_setup.virtual_user: guest signup once, WebSocket login, random match, one message every 3 s for a 60 s session, partner times the delivery, end the chat, queue again
test_setup.gateway_signup_limits: raised to 1,000,000 for the runs and restored after
test_setup.script_and_runner: loadtest/k6/chat.js and loadtest/run.sh (the runner's wait loop was fixed between runs A and B; no measurement changed)
test_setup.watchdog: stopped the run on any pod restart, a change in node count or node memory above 93 percent; it did not fire
